- When sentiment turns negative (especially >0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for downward pressure.  
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a forecasted rebound, cap the rebound at 10–15% below the peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect trend correction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish (0.00–0.67) but price has been trending downward, add a 3–5% downward bias to prevent over-optimism.  
- If forecasted price exceeds 85.00 and sentiment is neutral or bullish, apply a 5–8% downward adjustment to avoid overestimating upside.  
- For 30-day forecasts with strong recent volatility (e.g., >30% swing in last 5 days), reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to reflect uncertainty.
